messages:
alex: ran a quick nsys capture on the latest canary (kv-prefetch + new batching window). attaching top-line numbers, a bit surprising :thinking_face:

maria: saw it — can you paste the top kernels by self-time?

alex: sure, top 5 from the summary (nsys):
- attention_kernel_v2 42.1%
- kv_lookup_prefetch 18.7%
- softmax_fused 9.4%
- transpose_shard 6.2%
- layernorm_fwd 4.8%

kevin: attention dominating is expected but kv_lookup_prefetch at ~19% is high. are we seeing stalls in the KV path (L2 misses / long mem ops)?

maria: i pulled the timeline — long gaps between attention launches and KV returns at mid-sequence lengths (seq=1024). SM occupancy drops to ~26% during those gaps.

kevin: that occupancy dip + kv prefetch point to warp serialization on loads. could be uncoalesced accesses when prefetching too many keys in parallel.

alex: here's the exact capture command i ran:
```
nsys profile --output=canary_kv_prefetch_3301 --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,osrt --force-overwrite --duration=30
```

perf-bot: captured /artifacts/canary_kv_prefetch_3301.qdrep and available in perf dashboard. :robot_face:

sophie: quick idea — our prefetch adds N keys per batch window, maybe we overshoot when batch sizes jitter. if prefetch count scales with batch_size and batch_size hits a transient spike the memory fanout becomes huge.

maria: i inspected thread-level counters: L2 read throughput spikes right after prefetch ops then we see warp_stall_memory waiting ~12-15ms total across timeline slices.

kevin: propose two experiments: (1) cap prefetch per request to 8 keys and add randomized jitter between prefetch micro-batches, (2) fall back to on-demand KV lookup when batch_latency > X ms.

alex: +1. also want to test changing kernel selection for shorter sequences to a smaller attention kernel variant (attn_small) — it has lower launch overhead but worse perf at long seq, might help during occupancy dips.

sophie: i can land a canary that caps prefetch and toggles attn_small for seq <= 256. will run the same nsys profile and perfetto synthetic trace.

maria: for triage we should also produce a kernel-level hotlist CSV (kernel, total_time_ms, pct, avg_duration_us, occupancy). i'll generate that from the qdrep and attach.

alex: thanks — after those runs, let's run the microbench harness on Dedicated with synthetic traffic (seq sweep 64/256/1024) to see end-to-end latency and token cost.

kevin: note: if prefetch cap fixes the mem stalls but increases tail latency, we may need batching-engine backpressure (increase batch wait to fill more uniform windows). testing needed.

sophie: creating patch now, will tag @maria and @kevin for quick perf review. expected deploy to canary infra in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: action items summarized:
- sophie: canary patch (prefetch cap + attn_small toggle) — deploy to canary and run nsys (due: today EOD)
- alex: run microbench on Dedicated with seq sweep and collect cost/latency (due: tomorrow AM)
- kevin: prepare kernel hotlist script and occupancy extraction from qdrep (will attach script)
- all: reconvene after traces, aim to decide on permanent kernel-selection rule or prefetch heuristic tweak

alex: adding one more note — if we change kernel-selection heuristics, ensure model pinning respects version compatibility (don't auto-switch on Dedicated without rollout guard).

perf-bot: scheduled: canary_kv_prefetch_3301 follow-up trace in 35m, reminder will ping channel.

kevin: cool. i'll start drafting the hotlist CSV now and push a Gist for review.

alex: thanks all — feel free to drop short logs here, prefer tiny snippets rather than big dumps.

maria: uploaded initial hotlist: /artifacts/hotlist_canary_3301.csv (attn + kv entries top-heavy).

sophie: deployed canary, running nsys, ping when you see new artifacts. :rocket:
